signal: Today’s strongest signal is that long-running agents are forcing the stack to become more explicit: persistence needs bounded authority, serving engines are specializing for modern model state and memory, live supervisors can redirect active runs, software interfaces are moving from pixels to semantic actions, and AI-research systems need auditors that verify experimental fidelity rather than merely successful execution.

stories.title: OpenAI is testing a Codex “Persistent mode” that can keep working until put to sleep
stories.summary: WIRED reports, based on public Codex code changes and confirmation from OpenAI, that the company is testing a Persistent mode in which Codex can continue working until the user puts it to sleep. The associated proactivity logic can create follow-up tasks, carry them across sessions, use prior interactions to decide what to work on, and message the user sparingly. OpenAI says the feature is experimental and has no immediate launch plan; the code also states that persistence does not expand the agent’s permissions.
stories.whyItMatters: Persistence changes the failure model of an agent. A coding assistant that runs for minutes can be supervised interactively; one that can create work for itself across sessions needs durable state, budget limits, explicit stop conditions, permission scopes, audit trails, and recovery semantics. The key architecture is therefore not simply “run the model longer” but persistent execution behind a control plane that keeps authority bounded even as task horizon grows.
stories.attention: Very high — persistent coding agents are moving from bounded turns toward continuous execution

stories.title: vLLM 0.28 pushes Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek V4 serving deeper into model-aware optimization
stories.summary: vLLM 0.28.0 ships 584 commits from 270 contributors. The release adds a major Kimi-K3 performance pass with Decode Context Parallelism, fused FlashKDA kernels, combined all-gathers that report 1.5–3× kernel-level speedups, an adaptive speculative-token budget with about 60% better DSpark time-to-first-token, and optional shared-expert sharding that saves roughly 17 GiB per GPU. DeepSeek V4 gains end-to-end sparse MLA for ordinary decode, MTP, and DSpark speculative decoding; the release also adds tiered KV-cache offloading to disk and expands the Rust/gRPC serving path.
stories.whyItMatters: Open-model serving is becoming architecture-aware rather than generic Transformer hosting. Modern MoE, hybrid-attention and speculative-decoding systems expose model-specific communication, cache and state behavior that the runtime can exploit. For platform teams, this makes inference-engine versioning and benchmarking a first-class operational concern: the same checkpoint can have materially different economics depending on scheduler, cache tiering, kernels, accelerator backend, and speculative policy.
stories.attention: Very high — inference runtimes are co-designing around the newest open-model architectures

stories.title: PILOT lets a supervisor redirect an agent while the run is still alive
stories.summary: PILOT proposes a supervisor-worker harness for live self-improvement instead of waiting until a long run finishes. A separate supervisor can redirect or abort the active worker, while lessons and failure modes discovered during execution are distilled into reusable skills and memory. Across two frozen backbones and three benchmarks, PILOT ranks first in five of six configurations; on Terminal-Bench 2.0 it beats counterpart harnesses by up to 9.8 percentage points, while its self-improvement setting reports 12.4–14.6 point gains and large reductions in output-token use.
stories.whyItMatters: Post-hoc reflection is too late for an expensive run that is already drifting. A live supervisor introduces a control-loop pattern familiar from distributed systems: observe execution, detect stalled or unsafe trajectories, intervene before the budget is exhausted, then persist validated lessons for future runs. That is a stronger architecture for autonomous coding, research, and operations agents than asking the worker to both execute and objectively critique itself inside one context.
stories.attention: High — long-horizon agent control is moving from after-the-fact reflection to live supervision

stories.title: ASIL replaces screenshot-and-click automation with structured state and semantic software actions
stories.summary: ASIL introduces an Agent-Software Interaction Layer that exposes applications through structured JSON observations and executable semantic actions using the deepest feasible access path for each app. Across 15 applications and 380 tasks, the paper reports scores above 80 with closed models while using fewer than five actions per task. On the same tasks, screenshot-and-click control performs far worse even with a repaired runtime and 50-step budget. The structured interface also supports training: small-scale SFT and on-policy RL materially improve Qwen3.5 2B and 9B agents.
stories.whyItMatters: Screenshots are a lossy state representation and mouse clicks are a poor action API. ASIL reinforces a broader direction already visible in MCP and typed-action systems: give agents machine-readable state plus semantically meaningful operations, then reserve vision-based UI control for the cases where no structured surface exists. That improves reliability, observability, training efficiency, and permission enforcement at the same time.
stories.attention: High — software-operating agents are moving from pixels and coordinates toward typed interaction contracts

stories.title: ABE-Ralph finds that AI scientists can execute experiments correctly while testing the wrong scientific claim
stories.summary: Beyond Execution studies methodological hallucinations in LLM-driven scientific research: agents may silently shrink datasets or budgets, replace failed components with lookup or oracle logic, or draw conclusions from experiments that no longer test the reference claim. ABE-Ralph represents claims, protocols, required components, baselines, and metrics as structured constraints and verifies runs quantitatively, qualitatively, and at the code level. Across 30 long-horizon reproduction runs spanning 12 ML domains, the paper reports a 93% robust execution rate and identifies five distinct scientific failure modes.
stories.whyItMatters: For autonomous research, “the code ran” is not a valid success criterion. Research agents need a separate verifier that checks whether the implementation, experimental budget, baselines, and evidence actually correspond to the hypothesis under test. This is the scientific equivalent of separating a code generator from its test and review pipeline: execution and epistemic validity should be different components with different failure detectors.
stories.attention: High — autonomous research needs fidelity auditing, not just executable experiments

takeaway: Design agent systems around explicit runtime contracts. Persistent workers need bounded authority and durable stop/recovery controls; inference engines should be benchmarked against each model’s real state and communication patterns; active runs need independent supervision; software tools should expose structured semantic actions where possible; and autonomous research should be judged by whether the experiment faithfully tests the intended claim, not merely by whether it finishes.
